# Stat

Figma: [04f. Stat](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-916) · Family: 04 Data Display · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-02

A presentation component for a single numeric KPI - value, label, optional leading icon, optional delta indicator (embedded StatusPill), optional helper text. Three sizes (sm for tables and dense dashboards, md for standard cards, lg for hero KPIs), two layouts (vertical for cards, horizontal for inline rows), bilingual (LTR + RTL). Distinct from Chart (visualizes data over time) - Stat is for a single point-in-time number with light context.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/stat/reference.png`

### Stat

One headline KPI with label, display-size value, optional icon, optional delta StatusPill and optional helper text, for example Total invested 1.2M with ↑ 12% vs last quarter.

Level: molecule · Contains: StatusPill

Use when:
- Portfolio summary numbers: total invested, expected return, distributions received
- Hero metric on a deal page such as expected return 12.5% (Size=lg)
- A grid of 2 to 4 dashboard KPIs, one Stat each
- Back-office overview tiles (active deals, investors)

Don't use when:
- Lookup details in a list (issuance ID, maturity, profit rate): use KeyValue
- A value over time: use Chart / Line or Chart / KPI strip
- A categorical status: use StatusPill
- Funding progress toward a target: use ProgressBar
- The portfolio balance header with hide toggle: use PortfolioHeader

Accessibility: Read label then value then delta; announce delta direction in words ("up 12 percent"), not by color.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Stat presents a single numeric KPI with light context - the kind of pattern that shows up everywhere on financial dashboards, deal cards, portfolio summaries, and operational consoles. It's deliberately scoped to ONE number per instance. If you need to show several KPIs, render multiple Stat instances in a layout (Stats grid). If you need to show change over time, that's a Chart, not a Stat.

The value is the dominant element - bigger and bolder than everything else. The label says what the number is, the optional delta says how it's trending, the optional helper says when or in what context. Designers control which pieces are present via boolean variant axes (HasIcon, HasDelta, HasHelperText) so they only show what adds information.

### Family at a glance

> **Tip:** When to reach for Stat vs Chart vs StatusPill: Stat = single number with light context. Chart = number over time (sparkline, line, bar). StatusPill = categorical attribute label (Verified, Active, Pending). They compose - Stat embeds a StatusPill for the delta, and a future dashboard layout will arrange multiple Stats with a Chart underneath.

### Anatomy

Five elements, three of which are optional. The value and label are always present; the icon, delta, and helper text are toggled via boolean variant axes. Each element binds to its own token so swapping themes recolors everything in one place.

Value

The dominant numeric element. Display-scale type (20/24 for sm, 32/40 for md, 48/56 for lg) bound to text/default. Semi Bold for sm/md, Bold for lg. Number formatting is done in code (commas, currency symbols, percent signs) - the Figma component just shows display strings.

Label

Short noun phrase describing what the value represents - "Total invested", "Active deals", "Expected return". Bound to text/muted, Medium weight, 12-14px depending on size. Sits ABOVE the value in vertical layouts, beside the value in horizontal layouts.

Icon (optional)

Leading visual cue for category recognition - chart for analytics KPIs, wallet for financial totals, calendar for time-based metrics. Default Icon/chart-analytics. INSTANCE_SWAP planned for v2.1 (currently the icon is hardcoded - see Notes section). Sized 16/20/24px to match the Stat size.

Delta (optional, embedded StatusPill)

Embedded StatusPill instance showing change vs. a prior period. Defaults to Tone=success, Variant=subtle, with the up-arrow + percent ("↑ 12%"). Designers swap the StatusPill variant per-instance to use error tone for negative deltas, warning for neutral-but-attention-needed, etc. Size of the delta pill scales with the Stat (sm for sm/md Stats, md for lg Stats).

Helper text (optional)

Smaller context line below the value/delta - "vs. last month", "Q3 2026", "as of yesterday". Bound to text/subtle, Regular weight, 11-13px. Use to say WHEN the value applies or how it compares.

> **Info:** All five elements composed: a full Stat with icon + label + value + delta + helper. This is the "everything on" variant - use sparingly because each additional piece adds visual weight. Default to the minimum that conveys the information.

### Size - sm vs md vs lg

Size is THE most important decision for Stat. It picks how prominent the value should be and how much space it takes. Most KPIs sit in md. Hero KPIs go to lg. Dense dashboard rows go to sm.

Size = sm

· Value 20/24 semibold · label 12/16 · helper 11/14

· Icon 16px · embedded delta = StatusPill sm

· Use in table cells, sidebar metrics, compact KPI strips

· Example: "Active deals · 47" in a portfolio sidebar

Size = md

· Value 32/40 semibold · label 13/16 · helper 12/16

· Icon 20px · embedded delta = StatusPill sm

· DEFAULT. Use in dashboard cards, deal summaries, profile overviews

· Example: "Total invested · 1.2M ﷼ · ↑12%" on a deal page

Size = lg

· Value 48/56 BOLD · label 14/20 · helper 13/18

· Icon 24px · embedded delta = StatusPill md

· Use for hero KPIs that should be the focal point of a page

· Example: "Expected return · 12.5%" as the dominant metric on a deal hero

### Layout - vertical vs horizontal

Two layouts cover the two most common Stat placements. Vertical is the dashboard-card default - label on top, value bigger below, delta and helper trail. Horizontal compresses everything into a single row - useful for dense list rows, inline metric strips, and stats-as-row patterns.

Layout = vertical

Children stack top-down: optional icon, then label, then value (with optional delta to the right), then optional helper. The default and most common layout. Reads as a coherent block.

Layout = horizontal

Children stack left-to-right: optional icon, then a small text block (label above value with optional helper), then optional delta. Useful for inline KPI strips and list rows. Reads as a single horizontal item.

### Delta - embedded StatusPill

When HasDelta=true, an embedded StatusPill instance shows change vs. a prior period. The default is Tone=success, Variant=subtle - green pill with up-arrow indicating positive change. Designers swap the StatusPill variant per-instance to communicate different deltas.

### Common delta variants

> **Info:** Positive delta (default): Tone=success, content "↑ 12%" (LTR) / "12%" (RTL). Use for KPIs where higher is better - total invested, ROI, active deals, distributions received.

> **Info:** Negative delta: change StatusPill to Tone=error, content "↓ 3%". Use for KPIs where higher-is-better and the number went down (e.g. ROI fell), OR where lower-is-better and the number went up (e.g. defaulted deals increased).

> **Info:** Neutral delta: change StatusPill to Tone=neutral, content "0%" or "-". Use when there is no change or when the change is too small to be meaningful.

> **Info:** Warning delta: change StatusPill to Tone=warning, content "↑ 30%". Use when the change is large enough to warrant attention regardless of direction (sudden spike in late payments, or unexpected drop in distributions).

> **Warning:** The DEFAULT delta pill in every Stat variant is Tone=success, Variant=subtle. This is intentional - most dashboard deltas are positive (companies build dashboards to show growth). For negative deltas, the calling code switches the StatusPill's tone - it does NOT detach the Stat instance.

### Icon - category recognition

When HasIcon=true, a leading icon reinforces the KPI category at a glance - chart for analytics, wallet for financial totals, calendar for time-based metrics, users for headcount. The default is Icon/chart-analytics - a generic visual cue that the value is a metric.

> **Warning:** In v2.0 the icon is hardcoded to chart-analytics - it is NOT an INSTANCE_SWAP property yet. This is on the v2.1 roadmap. For now, designers who need a different icon must detach the Stat instance and swap the icon manually (NOT preferred - creates silent drift). If a different icon is critical, file a request to add INSTANCE_SWAP support sooner.

In vertical layouts the icon sits ABOVE the label, occupying its own row. In horizontal layouts the icon sits LEFT of the text block (or right for RTL). Icon size scales with Stat size: 16px for sm, 20px for md, 24px for lg.

### Direction - LTR + RTL

Every variant exists in LTR (English, IBM Plex Sans) and RTL (Arabic, Noto Sans Arabic) directions. RTL reverses child order - icon trails to the right, delta sits to the left of the value, helper text right-aligns. Auto-layout handles the flip; designers don't mirror anything manually.

LTR →

RTL →

> **Tip:** Number formatting in RTL: the value itself is shown in Arabic-Indic digits OR Western digits depending on locale and convention. Saudi financial apps typically use Western digits ("1,250,000") for consistency with international standards, paired with the Riyal icon (﷼) as the trailing currency symbol. The Stat component doesn't force a digit style; the calling code provides the value as a string and the Riyal icon is appended via the value-with-currency frame.

> **Info:** Currency placement in RTL: "1.2 مليون ﷼" (1.2 million Riyals) - the Riyal icon sits at the end (left side visually in RTL because Arabic reads right-to-left, so the unit naturally trails the number when reading). For percent: "12.5%" - the % sign stays attached to the digit in both directions. The Figma component embeds the Riyal icon next to the value text inside a "value-with-currency" horizontal frame.

> **Warning:** Font fallback (same as Badge, Tooltip, StatusPill): Noto Sans Arabic Medium for Arabic. IBM Plex Sans Arabic is not installed in this Figma file. If installed later, regenerate all RTL variants.

### Content guidance

Stat is most useful when each piece of content earns its place. Keep the bar high - every additional element costs visual weight.

### Value formatting

- Currency: use the Riyal icon (﷼) trailing the value for Saudi Riyals - "1.2M ﷼" not just "1.2M" and not "1.2M SAR". For large amounts use abbreviated forms (K, M, B); for amounts under 10,000 show the full number with thousand separators. For non-SAR currencies (USD, EUR, GBP) use the text suffix ("$1.2M", "€850K") - the icon is reserved for Riyal.
- Percentages: show ONE decimal place for ROI-like numbers ("12.5%"), no decimals for whole-percent rates ("47%"). Don't show "12.50%" - the trailing zero adds noise.
- Counts: comma thousand separators for English ("1,247"), Arabic locale separators for Arabic ("١٬٢٤٧" if using Arabic-Indic digits, or "1,247" if using Western digits in RTL).
- Dates: prefer relative ("2 days ago") over absolute ("2026-06-02") for human-readable Stats. Use absolute when precision matters (e.g. "as of 14:00 today" for live-updating dashboards).

### Label conventions

- Use sentence case for English: "Total invested", "Active deals". Don't use title case ("Total Invested") in Safqah's style.
- Keep labels under 4 words. Long labels wrap awkwardly in horizontal layouts and create awkward whitespace in vertical layouts.
- Don't repeat units in the label and the value. "Total invested" → "1.2M ﷼", NOT "Total invested (SAR)" → "1.2M ﷼". The Riyal icon trailing the value carries the currency meaning; the label says what the value represents.

### Helper text patterns

- "vs. last [period]" - for delta-supported KPIs. "vs. last month", "vs. last quarter", "vs. last year".
- "[date range]" - for fixed-period KPIs. "Q3 2026", "Year-to-date", "Since launch".
- "as of [time]" - for live-updating KPIs. "as of 14:00", "as of yesterday", "live".
- Skip helper text entirely if it duplicates the context that's already on the page. If the page is "Q3 Dashboard", "Q3 2026" in every Stat is noise.

### Code examples - Flutter

Reference implementations. Real production code lives in lib/design_system/stat/.

### Basic usage

```dart
// Minimal stat - just label and value
SafqahStat(
  label: 'Active deals',
  value: '47',
)

// Standard dashboard card with currency icon + delta + helper
// The Riyal icon is rendered automatically when currency == 'SAR'
SafqahStat(
  label: 'Total invested',
  value: '1.2M',
  currency: SafqahCurrency.sar,  // renders the Riyal icon after the value
  size: StatSize.md,
  delta: StatusPillVariant.success(label: '↑ 12%'),
  helper: 'vs. last quarter',
  hasIcon: true,
)

// Hero KPI on deal page - percent value, no currency
SafqahStat(
  label: 'Expected return',
  value: '12.5%',
  size: StatSize.lg,
  delta: StatusPillVariant.success(label: '↑ 0.3pp'),
  helper: 'Annualized · Q3 2026',
)

// Non-SAR currency uses text suffix (no icon)
SafqahStat(
  label: 'USD reserves',
  value: '$450K',  // dollar sign inline
  size: StatSize.md,
  delta: StatusPillVariant.success(label: '↑ 4%'),
)

// Horizontal stat row (dense layout)
SafqahStat(
  label: 'Active deals',
  value: '47',
  size: StatSize.sm,
  layout: StatLayout.horizontal,
  delta: StatusPillVariant.success(label: '↑ 5'),
  hasIcon: true,
)
```

### Number formatting (currency + locale)

```dart
// File: lib/design_system/stat/value_formatter.dart
import 'package:intl/intl.dart';

class StatValueFormatter {
  /// Format a numeric value for display. The currency unit (Riyal icon for SAR,
  /// text suffix for others) is rendered by SafqahStat, not by the formatter.
  /// This function returns the digit string only.
  static String currency(num value, {
    Locale? locale,
    bool abbreviated = false,
  }) {
    final loc = locale?.toString() ?? 'en';
    if (abbreviated && value.abs() >= 1000000) {
      final m = (value / 1000000).toStringAsFixed(1);
      return loc.startsWith('ar') ? '$m مليون' : '${m}M';
    }
    final formatter = NumberFormat.decimalPattern(loc);
    return formatter.format(value);
  }

  /// Format a percentage. Default: 1 decimal for sub-unity, 0 for whole.
  static String percent(num value, {int decimals = 1}) {
    if (value == value.roundToDouble() && decimals == 1) {
      return '${value.toInt()}%';
    }
    return '${value.toStringAsFixed(decimals)}%';
  }

  /// Format an integer count with locale-appropriate separators.
  static String count(int value, {Locale? locale}) {
    final formatter = NumberFormat.decimalPattern(locale?.toString() ?? 'en');
    return formatter.format(value);
  }
}

// SafqahStat consumer code:
// SafqahStat(
//   label: 'Total invested',
//   value: StatValueFormatter.currency(1250000, abbreviated: true), // "1.2M"
//   currency: SafqahCurrency.sar,  // appends Riyal icon
// )
```

### Delta with auto-tone derivation

```dart
// File: lib/design_system/stat/delta.dart
// Helper to derive the right StatusPill tone from a numeric delta.
// Caller picks "higher is better" or "lower is better" semantic - the helper
// returns the right tone + direction arrow.
class StatDelta {
  static StatusPillVariant fromChange({
    required num change,
    required String unit,  // '%', 'pp', 'deals', etc
    bool higherIsBetter = true,
  }) {
    if (change == 0) {
      return StatusPillVariant.neutral(label: '-');
    }
    final arrow = change > 0 ? '↑' : '↓';
    final isPositive = (change > 0) == higherIsBetter;
    final tone = isPositive ? StatusPillTone.success : StatusPillTone.error;
    final magnitude = change.abs().toStringAsFixed(unit == '%' ? 1 : 0);
    return StatusPillVariant(
      tone: tone,
      label: '$arrow $magnitude$unit',
      hasIcon: false,  // arrow character carries direction
    );
  }
}

// Usage:
// SafqahStat(
//   label: 'Total invested',
//   value: '1.2M SAR',
//   delta: StatDelta.fromChange(change: 12.5, unit: '%'),
// )
```

### Do and Don't

Five pairs of operational guidance for Stat usage.

### One number per Stat

- **Do** · Scenario name: Render each KPI as its own Stat instance. For a dashboard, lay out multiple Stats in a grid. Each Stat has one label and one value.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't cram multiple numbers into a single Stat value ("47 deals · 12 late"). If you have two numbers, you have two Stats - split them.

### Match size to importance

- **Do** · Scenario name: Hero KPI on a deal page → lg. Standard dashboard card → md. Inline table row metric → sm. Pick the size that matches how prominent the number should be in the layout.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't use lg everywhere because the number "feels important". If every Stat is lg, nothing stands out. lg is for the focal point of a screen.

### Use delta only when comparison exists

- **Do** · Scenario name: Show a delta when there's a meaningful prior-period value to compare to ("vs. last month"). The delta is the change from that prior value.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't fabricate deltas. If there's no prior period yet (new investor, new account, first month), skip HasDelta=true. A "↑ 0%" delta is meaningless.

### Helper text earns its place

- **Do** · Scenario name: Use helper text when it adds context the value alone can't convey - the time period, the comparison baseline, when the data was last refreshed.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't use helper text to repeat what's already on the page. If the page header says "Q3 2026", helper text in every Stat saying "Q3 2026" is noise.

### Negative deltas use error tone

- **Do** · Scenario name: For a KPI where higher is better, a negative change uses Tone=error on the StatusPill ("↓ 3%" in red). For lower-is-better KPIs (late payments), a positive change uses Tone=error.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't leave a negative delta in the default Tone=success (green). The color carries meaning - green for a drop in distributions would actively mislead users.

### Notes from the maintainer

Design decisions, known gaps, and constraints for the next maintainer.

> **Info:** Delta is an EMBEDDED StatusPill instance, not a separate axis. This means the delta inherits all 96 StatusPill variants (tone, variant, size, hasIcon, direction) - designers swap the StatusPill's tone per-instance to communicate positive/negative/neutral deltas. The Stat component encodes the SPACE for the delta; the StatusPill encodes the STATE of the delta.

> **Warning:** Icon is hardcoded to chart-analytics in v2.0. INSTANCE_SWAP is on the v2.1 roadmap - currently if designers need a different icon (wallet for financial totals, calendar for time-based metrics), they must detach the Stat instance. Discouraged - file a request to add INSTANCE_SWAP support if a real use case appears.

> **Info:** Number formatting is RUNTIME, not design-time. The Figma component shows display strings ("1.2M") with the Riyal icon embedded in the value-with-currency wrapping frame. Production code uses Dart intl NumberFormat with locale-aware separators, then renders the value text alongside the Riyal SVG asset. See Code Examples for the StatValueFormatter pattern.

> **Info:** Delta tone auto-derivation lives in Flutter, not in the Figma variants. The Stat component has the SPACE for a delta StatusPill but doesn't pick its tone - the calling code derives positive/negative based on the change direction and the higher-is-better/lower-is-better semantic of the KPI. The Figma default (Tone=success) is just the most common starting point.

> **Info:** No dark mode yet. Stat has Light-mode-only bindings (same as Badge, Tooltip, StatusPill). The semantic tokens it binds to (text/default, text/muted, text/subtle) DO have dark mode definitions, so adding dark mode is mostly a verification exercise rather than a redesign.

> **Info:** No sparkline / mini chart in v2.0. The trend indicator is the delta StatusPill - communicates direction + magnitude without taking pixel real estate for a chart. Sparklines come in a future iteration, likely as a separate Chart component that composes alongside Stat.

> **Tip:** Arabic font fallback: Noto Sans Arabic Medium (regular and bold) - same as the rest of Syntropy. IBM Plex Sans Arabic is not installed in this Figma file. Note: Noto Sans Arabic uses "SemiBold" (no space) for its semibold weight while IBM Plex Sans uses "Semi Bold" (with space) - there's a fontStyle resolver in the build code that maps per family.

> **Tip:** In horizontal layouts, the icon AND delta both sit beside the text block. For RTL, this means the icon trails to the right and the delta sits to the left of the text block (or right, depending on auto-layout order). Auto-layout handles the flip via reversed child order in the build code.

> **Warning:** Don't detach Stat instances to customize the icon or change the layout. If a real use case appears for a different icon, file a request to add INSTANCE_SWAP. If a real use case appears for a different layout (e.g. value-above-label inverted), file a request to add a Layout option. Detached instances break design system audit and create silent drift.
